title: JDK, JRE, and Types of Errors

blocks.value: The Java Development Kit (JDK) is the full toolkit for writing, compiling, and debugging Java programs. The Java Runtime Environment (JRE) is just what's needed to run an already-compiled Java program.

Syntax errors are invalid statements the compiler catches while compiling — for example, a missing semicolon. The compiler reports an error message, and you have to find and fix the mistake before the program will compile.

Logical errors are different: the program compiles and runs fine, but produces the wrong result — for example, a program meant to add two numbers that multiplies them instead. Logical errors don't produce error messages, so they're harder to catch — you have to notice the output is wrong and trace back to the cause yourself.
